searchText: I agree > Any updates on the testnet? There was one started right? <@!118185622543269890> There is one started indeed. It is not definitive since we still have consensus issues between Geth and Besu. This is a clique network, currently the block period is 15 seconds. You can start playing with it if you want, there are 3 Besu nodes running. You can submit legacy and EIP-1559 transactions. The block explorer is here: http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/ The network status is here: http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3001/ RPC endpoints: http://13.236.147.35:8545 http://18.222.108.145:8545 http://15.188.238.162:8545 Awesome!! Thank you Configuration files are here: https://github.com/PegaSysEng/eip1559-testnet/tree/master/config Will definitely toy with it soon 404 On the config link Try again please Working, thanks! Keeping this on the down low or is it fine if I make a tweet when I toy with it? Might try spamming high gas tx's or something lol I would say it is fine. Even if we know it is not stable yet. But definitely feel free to play with it. Maybe just don't put urls in your tweet 👍 Sounds good, thanks again, really excited Any analyzes on correlation between ETH price and revenue from fees? I know that when ETH swings, txs tend to increase (especially with DeFi) temporarily, but seems like historically fees long term volatility is pretty decoupled from ETH price. This is good for ETH2.0 since revenue from fees shouldn't be affected too much by ETH price crashing, ensuring stakers still profit from their revenue. EIP-1559 will eat most of this revenue however, which means ETH2.0 security will be almost entirely based on ETH price, making ETH price volatility more dangerous for the security of the chain. > <@!132827600492953600> haydenadams on the uniswap discord <@!132827600492953600> I wrote to Hayden, if we have a concrete proposal he'll listen to it, but they don't have any solutions in the works, due to the UX impact. It would be *far* simpler to just have Geth price-time order transactions rather than price-random order transactions. Every backrunner would throw their hat into the ring once as fast as they could and that would be it. Whoever is most well connected will win.

excerpts.author: phabc
excerpts.content:
Any analyzes on correlation between ETH price and revenue from fees? I know that when ETH swings, txs tend to increase (especially with DeFi) temporarily, but seems like historically fees long term volatility is pretty decoupled from ETH price.

This is good for ETH2.0 since revenue from fees shouldn't be affected too much by ETH price crashing, ensuring stakers still profit from their revenue. EIP-1559 will eat most of this revenue however, which means ETH2.0 security will be almost entirely based on ETH price, making ETH price volatility more dangerous for the security of the chain.
